citation.title: Mechanostat-type effective density correction for Carter-Hayes growth applied to topology optimization and its efficient interpolation for a target strain energy and volume fraction
citation.authors: Luis Irastorza-Valera, Ricardo Larraínzar-Garijo, Javier Montoya-Adárraga, Luis Saucedo-Mora
citation.version_coded: arXiv v1 (27 Mar 2025), HTML full text; v1 is the only version; no version of record found (web search 2026-09-24)

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: A small physics-loss network (D2NN), trained for 500 epochs on 20 topology images, gives designs said to resemble 2,000 iterations of the authors' non-learned logarithmic SIMP scheme; once trained, a roughly 25-fold speed-up is claimed.
claim.key_phrase: similar results to 2,000 steps worth of vanilla iteration within 500 training epochs
claim.location: abstract, paragraph 3; the speed-up factor is stated in Sec. 7 (discussion of Fig. 18)
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Stated in Sec. 7 for the trained D2NN versus the vanilla scheme. No times are printed for either method, so the factor cannot be re-derived. The abstract's 2,000 iterations versus 500 training epochs compares effort in different units and is not a time ratio.
claim.alternatives: (1) Sec. 7: running 5 iterations of Eq. 15 after the D2NN prediction is said to bring the result closer to the 2,000-iteration reference; no time given. (2) Abstract, last sentence: the ML surrogate is described qualitatively as quick and low-cost. (3) Sec. 6.1 (non-ML): the erosion filter is said to add no noticeable cost; the filtered cantilever run (1000x200 per the Fig. 2 caption) reached iteration 1000 in about 1.5 h on a single-core i7 1.8 GHz with 16 GB RAM.

baseline.classical_method: The authors' own non-learned scheme, termed the vanilla iteration: SIMP compliance minimization built on top88.m, with the mechanostat-type logarithmic volume update (Eq. 15) and the twigcutter erosion filter (Sec. 2-3, Algorithm 1)
baseline.implementation: MATLAB top88.m, the 88-line educational code (ref. [1]), plus the authors' twigcutter.m (Sec. 3); D2NN framework not stated
baseline.solver: not stated [inferred: top88.m solves with MATLAB sparse backslash, a direct solver; recalled from the public top88 code, not stated in the article]
baseline.hardware_classical: single-core i7 1.8 GHz, 16 GB RAM (Sec. 6.1); stated for the filtered Fig. 8 cantilever run, not for the Sec. 7 comparison
baseline.problem_size: D2NN comparison: 600x200 cantilever (Sec. 7); timed classical run: the Fig. 8 cantilever, which the Fig. 2 caption identifies as the 1000x200 case of Sec. 3 [inferred link]
baseline.classical_iterations: Fixed 2,000 iterations for the reference designs (abstract; Sec. 7, Fig. 18). Algorithm 1 loops while the design change exceeds tol and the volume is below target; the tol value is not stated.
baseline.classical_time: not stated for the Sec. 7 comparison; about 1.5 h to iteration 1000 for the filtered 1000x200 cantilever [size via Fig. 2 caption, inferred link] (Sec. 6.1), i.e. about 5.4 s per iteration [derived: 1.5 h × 3600 s/h ÷ 1000]
baseline.ml_time: not stated; only the relative factor of about 25 (Sec. 7)
baseline.training_time: not stated; 500 epochs with Adam (Sec. 7, Algorithm 2)
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated; 20 training images produced by the vanilla scheme along volume-compliance curves, 10 with filter radius r = 1 and 10 with r = 4 per the Fig. 15-16 captions (Sec. 7)
baseline.quality_metric: Visual comparison of FEBio von Mises stress maps of D2NN outputs and 2,000-iteration references (Fig. 18); no compliance or volume values for D2NN outputs
baseline.quality_gap: not quantified; Sec. 7 concedes an inexact match because the training points lie on other volume-compliance curves than the target points

R1.evidence: Sec. 7, Fig. 18: quality parity with the 2,000-iteration reference rests on visual similarity of stress maps. No compliance or volume values are given for D2NN outputs. The reference uses a fixed iteration count with no stated convergence check, and the authors concede the match is inexact.

R2.evidence: Sec. 6.1, Sec. 7: hardware is given only for one classical run (single core, i7 1.8 GHz) and not for the D2NN or the Sec. 7 comparison; the baseline builds on the educational top88.m code. Markers (b)-(d) are not established: the article shows no convergence evidence for the 600x200 reference. R2(e) is not decidable yet: the derivable per-iteration time of the 1000x200 run (about 5.4 s [derived]) needs a same-size single-core strong-baseline measurement, and it belongs to a different problem than the primary outcome.

R3.evidence: Abstract, Sec. 7: training is counted only as 500 epochs, with no time. The cost of producing the 20 training topologies with the vanilla scheme itself is not reported, and no break-even is given.

R4.evidence: Sec. 7, Fig. 18: D2NN outputs are analysed in FEBio (stress maps), but no compliance, volume or constraint values and no failure count are reported. Only 4 target points plus the full block are shown.

reporting.n_test_cases: 4 target points (P1-P4) plus the full block, one 600x200 cantilever (Sec. 7, Figs. 17-18); 20 training images (Figs. 15-16)

notes: The classical comparator is the authors' own mechanostat-type SIMP variant, not standard SIMP. ood_test is unclear because Sec. 7 places P1-P2 inside and P3-P4 outside the training dataset while also calling all four unseen. The Sec. 7 text gives r = 1 for both halves of the training set, but the Fig. 16 caption gives r = 4 [typo inferred]. Only one classical runtime is reported (Sec. 6.1, a different problem), hence runtimes_all_cases = selective. No code or data statement. Figure images were not inspected; coding uses text and captions.
